title: Career Strategy Playbook
subtitle: Build, Navigate, and Future-Proof Your Career

sections.title: Why You Need a Career Strategy

blocks.text: Most professionals drift through careers, chasing the next promotion or job switch without a bigger picture. The result? Burnout, mismatched roles, and stagnation.

A career strategy ensures that every move—MBA, job switch, skill acquisition—aligns with your **long-term goals**. Think of it like financial planning: structured, intentional, and focused on compounding results.

blocks.label: Reflection
blocks.text: Do you currently make career moves reactively (chasing opportunities) or proactively (shaping opportunities)?
Ask yourself: What do I want my professional legacy to be?

items: Do you aspire to be a Partner at a consulting firm?
A Product Head driving tech innovation?

blocks.text: Your long-term vision guides short-term choices.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Write a 10-year vision statement for your career.
Big visions require milestones. Example:

items: **Short-Term (1–2 years):** Get into consulting via Big 4.
**Medium-Term (3–5 years):** Move to MBB or strategy role in Fortune 500.

blocks.label: Worksheet
blocks.text: Map 1 short-term and 1 medium-term milestone toward your vision.

sections.title: Identify Your Core Strengths & Development Areas

blocks.text: Clarity on your strengths lets you double down; clarity on weaknesses helps you upskill.
Framework:

items: Strengths = what you do better than peers.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Ask 3 colleagues: “What do I do best?” and “Where should I improve?” Note down themes.

sections.title: Map Your Career Against Market Trends

blocks.text: Industries evolve fast. Roles today may not exist tomorrow. Align your strategy with **future demand.**

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Identify 1 macro-trend in your industry. Write how you’ll align your career with it.

sections.title: Build a Personal Brand That Attracts Opportunities

blocks.text: Your brand = how the market perceives you. Build it by:
When recruiters Google you, they should see **evidence of expertise.**

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Write a 1-sentence “positioning statement” (e.g., Finance professional passionate about ESG investing).
Networking isn’t random—it’s targeted. Build **3 networks:**

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Make a list of 5 people you’ll reach out to this month.
Don’t learn everything. Learn strategically. Example:

items: Consultant? Learn AI strategy, data storytelling.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Pick 1 skill that boosts your long-term vision.

sections.title: Create a Career Portfolio, Not Just a Job History

blocks.text: A job is temporary. A **career portfolio** is the sum of your skills, networks, and projects. Build assets that outlive jobs: certifications, thought leadership, side hustles.

blocks.label: Reflection
blocks.text: What assets are you building beyond your current job?

sections.title: Plan for Career Pivots and Transitions

blocks.text: Few careers are linear. Be ready to pivot. Example:

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Write down one “Plan B” career path if your current plan doesn’t work out.

Rohit joined a Big Four firm after his MBA. With mentorship, he moved to a strategy consulting firm within 3 years. By strategically publishing LinkedIn insights on digital transformation, he built thought leadership and accelerated to Manager within 6 years.

blocks.label: Lesson
blocks.text: Career strategy = **intentional positioning + execution.**
Megha, a software engineer, realized coding wasn’t her long-term path. With guidance, she pursued a 1-year MBA, networked into a fintech startup, and now leads product strategy.

blocks.label: Lesson
blocks.text: Pivoting early + aligning skills = exponential growth.

items: Mistakes: Drifting without vision, ignoring trends, waiting for promotions.
Fix: Define vision, rebrand, network, upskill.
